ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a parallelogram whose oblique sides are consistent with the side directions of the regular hexagons, with two congruent unshaded regular hexagons inside, and the remaining region is shaded with diagonal lines. The upper and lower sides of the parallelogram are horizontal, and the left and right oblique sides are parallel to the 60-degree direction sides of the regular hexagons. The side lengths of the two regular hexagons are the same. Reasoning: Calculate the area by triangular grid. Let the common side length of the regular hexagons be 1 grid unit. From the alignment relationship of the sides in the figure, the outer parallelogram spans 4 side-length units in the horizontal direction and 3 side-length units in the oblique direction, so it can be divided into 4×3 identical rhombi. Each rhombus is equal to 2 small equilateral triangles, so the parallelogram has the area of 4×3×2=24 small equilateral triangles in total. Each regular hexagon is composed of 6 such small equilateral triangles, and the two regular hexagons together occupy 12 small triangles. The shaded part is the part of the parallelogram after removing these two regular hexagons, so the shaded area is 24−12=12 small triangles. The ratio of the shaded area to the area of the parallelogram is 12/24=1/2.

raw_record.question_text: In the figure, two regular hexagons are equal to each other. What part of the parallelogram's area is shaded?

method.method_draft: Use a triangular-lattice area count. From the image, read that the two unshaded equal regular hexagons have the same side length, and that all visible parallelogram edges are parallel to sides of the hexagons: the top and bottom are horizontal hexagon-edge directions, and the slanted sides follow the 60-degree hexagon-edge direction. Let the common hexagon side be one lattice unit. The outer parallelogram spans 4 side-lengths along the horizontal direction and 3 side-lengths along the slanted direction, so it is made of 4×3 congruent rhombi, each equal to 2 small equilateral triangles, for 24 small equilateral triangles total. Each regular hexagon is made of 6 such equilateral triangles, so the two hexagons occupy 12 of the 24 triangles. The shaded region is the complement, also 12 triangles, giving shaded fraction 12/24 = 1/2.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates and area formulas. From the image, take the common side length of each regular hexagon as s. The outer parallelogram’s horizontal base consists of four hexagon side-lengths, so its base is 4s. Its slanted side consists of three hexagon side-length steps in the 60-degree direction, giving vertical height 3·(sqrt(3)/2)s. Thus the parallelogram area is 4s · 3sqrt(3)s/2 = 6sqrt(3)s^2. One regular hexagon of side s has area 6·(sqrt(3)s^2/4)=3sqrt(3)s^2/2, so the two unshaded hexagons have area 3sqrt(3)s^2. Therefore the shaded area is 6sqrt(3)s^2 − 3sqrt(3)s^2 = 3sqrt(3)s^2, which is half the parallelogram area.
